en istap.explanation: "En istap" means "an icicle". It is built from "is" (ice) and "tap" (a peg). The part "is" also appears in "en isbjørn" (a polar bear).

en isterning.explanation: "En isterning" means "an ice cube". It is built from "is" (ice) and "en terning" (a cube). To talk about a die in a board game, the same word "terning" is used: "Jeg slår med terningen" (I roll the die).

en isvaffel.explanation: "En isvaffel" means "an ice cream cone". It is built from "is" (ice cream) and "en vaffel" (a waffle). To offer someone an ice cream, say: "Vil du have en is?" (Do you want an ice cream?)

en italiener.explanation: "En italiener" means "an Italian". To describe food or other things, use the matching word "italiensk": "italiensk mad" (Italian food). The same word names the language. To say you speak it, say: "Jeg taler italiensk" (I speak Italian).

en iværksætter.explanation: "En iværksætter" means "an entrepreneur". It is the noun for the verb "at iværksætte" (to set going). To say what someone does for a living, Danish leaves out "en": "Hun er iværksætter" (She is an entrepreneur).

et ildfast fad.explanation: "Et ildfast fad" means "an ovenproof dish". It is "et fad" (a dish) with the adjective "ildfast" (fireproof) in front. The part "ild" (fire) also appears in "en ildslukker" (a fire extinguisher).

et imperium.explanation: "Et imperium" means "an empire". The shorter word "et rige" (a realm) is also used for an empire. To name the Roman one, say: "Romerriget" (the Roman Empire).

et indbrud.explanation: "Et indbrud" means "a burglary". It is built from "ind" (in) and "et brud" (a break). The part "brud" also appears in "et benbrud" (a broken bone). To say a burglary has happened, say: "Der har været indbrud hos naboen" (There has been a burglary at the neighbor's).

et indkøb.explanation: "Et indkøb" means "a purchase". It is built from "ind" (in) and "køb" (purchase). To say you need to buy groceries, say: "Jeg skal lave indkøb" (I need to do the shopping).

et indkøbscenter.explanation: "Et indkøbscenter" means "a shopping mall". It is built from "indkøb" (shopping) and "et center" (a center). The word "et shoppingcenter" (a shopping mall) means the same.

et indlæg.explanation: "Et indlæg" means "a post / contribution". To talk about something you publish online, say: "et indlæg på Facebook" (a post on Facebook). To say someone gives a short talk at a meeting, say: "Hun holdt et indlæg i mødet" (She gave a talk at the meeting).

et indtryk.explanation: "Et indtryk" means "an impression". To say something affected you strongly, say: "Det gjorde stort indtryk på mig" (It made a big impression on me). Do not mix it up with "et udtryk" (an expression). To talk about a phrase, say: "et sjovt udtryk" (a funny expression).

et initiativ.explanation: "Et initiativ" means "an initiative". To say someone is good at starting things, say: "Han har meget initiativ" (He has a lot of initiative). To say you did something without being asked, say: "Hun gjorde det på eget initiativ" (She did it on her own initiative).

et insekt.explanation: "Et insekt" means "an insect". It is the first part of "et insektbid" (an insect bite), built from "insekt" and "bid" (a bite). To say you have been bitten, say: "Jeg har et insektbid på armen" (I have an insect bite on my arm).

et instinkt.explanation: "Et instinkt" means "an instinct". To say someone is naturally good at something, say: "Han har et godt instinkt for fodbold" (He has a good instinct for football).

et institut.explanation: "Et institut" means "an institute". At a Danish university, a department is called "et institut": "Institut for Datalogi" (the Department of Computer Science). A beauty salon is "et skønhedsinstitut" (a beauty institute).

et instrument.explanation: "Et instrument" means "an instrument". To ask whether someone plays music, say: "Spiller du et instrument?" (Do you play an instrument?) To talk about a tool for measuring, say "et måleinstrument" (a measuring instrument).

et interview.explanation: "Et interview" means "an interview". To say you interview someone, use "at interviewe" (to interview): "Journalisten skal interviewe ministeren" (The journalist will interview the minister). For an interview for a job, use "en jobsamtale" (a job interview): "Jeg har en jobsamtale i morgen" (I have a job interview tomorrow).

i.explanation: "I" means "you". To speak to several people at once, use "I" as the subject: "Er I trætte?" (Are you all tired?) Do not mix it up with "i" (in), which sounds the same: "i huset" (in the house).

i aften.explanation: "I aften" means "this evening". To say what you will do later today, say: "Jeg ser en film i aften" (I am watching a movie this evening). To talk about the evening that has already ended, use "i aftes" (last night): "Jeg så en film i aftes" (I watched a movie last night).

i aftes.explanation: "I aftes" means "last night / yesterday evening". To say what you did the evening before, say: "Jeg så en film i aftes" (I watched a movie last night). Do not mix it up with "i aften" (this evening), which is the evening still to come: "Jeg ser en film i aften" (I am watching a movie this evening).

i dag.explanation: "I dag" means "today". It is written as two words, unlike the English word. Literally, it is "in day". To ask what someone is doing today, say: "Hvad skal du lave i dag?" (What are you doing today?)

i det hele taget.explanation: "I det hele taget" means "on the whole". To say you like something in general, say: "Jeg kan i det hele taget godt lide det" (I generally like it). To ask whether something is possible at all, use it in a question: "Kan du i det hele taget svømme?" (Can you swim at all?)

i det mindste.explanation: "I det mindste" means "at least". Literally, it is "in the smallest". To say something is still good in a bad situation, say: "Hun er syg, men hun har i det mindste ikke feber" (She is sick, but at least she has no fever).

i det store hele.explanation: "I det store hele" means "all in all". Literally, it is "in the big whole". To sum up your overall view even though some things were bad, say: "I det store hele var turen god, men hotellet var dårligt" (All in all the trip was good, but the hotel was bad).
